chapters.title: Opening
text: The Balkan Confederation in five minutes.
Naš dom: Our home.

chapters.title: The States
text: From the Julian Alps to the shores of the Black Sea, one language of a thousand faces.
Founded neither on blood nor on the rule of the most numerous, but on the will to live together.
48 territorial States, each attached to one of the seven constituent peoples.

4 confederal territories, the four capitals, which share the institutions of the Confederation. Zagreb, judicial capital; Beograd, economic capital; Sarajevo, political capital; Sofija, defence and sciences.
+ 2 autonomous municipalities. Brčko and Mostar, under confederal jurisdiction; they are not States.
Every State is sovereign, except where the Constitution limits it. Borders fixed at the founding.

chapters.title: The peoples
text: Seven constituent peoples: Slovenci (Slovenes), Hrvati (Croats), Srbi (Serbs), Bošñaci (Bosniaks), Crnogorci (Montenegrins), Makedonci (Macedonians), Bãlgari (Bulgarians).
Belonging is a personal choice. From the age of eighteen, every citizen may join the national register of the people of his choice.
No one is compelled to declare. A citizen in no register keeps every civic right: he votes for the Kongres and in referendums.
Your State is the State of your commune. Attachment follows residence, never a free choice. The register decides only the vote for the Narodni Sabor.

And all the communities who share this land. 24 autonomous entities protect those who are a minority where they live. The Albanian, Hungarian, Slovak and Turkish communities sit together in the Council of Communities.
“Naš dom” in the languages of the communities: Náš domov, Otthonunk, Yuvamız, Shtëpia jonë.

chapters.title: The institutions
text: The Kongres, the citizens. 250 delegates elected in every State in proportion to its population, from 2 to 20 seats per State.
The Narodni Sabor, the peoples. Seven delegations of ten. Each people elects its own, wherever its members live.
The Konfederalno Veće, the executive. Seven councillors, one per people. They decide by consensus, or failing that by a qualified majority.
The Ustavni Sud, the guardian. The Constitutional Court, in Zagreb, ensures that confederal law respects the Constitution.
Three of them sit in Sarajevo. The Kongres, the Narodni Sabor and the Konfederalno Veće in the political capital; the Ustavni Sud in Zagreb.

chapters.title: How a law is made
text: A law starts in the Kongres. A simple majority of the delegates present adopts it.

Laws on identity need the peoples. Languages and the alphabet, schools, culture, symbols, borders, memory: the Narodni Sabor must consent, by a majority in plenary and in five of its seven delegations.
Five of seven is not enough. The five must also represent a majority of the citizens enrolled in the national registers: the double key.
Six of seven, 75 % of registered citizens. Neither the smaller peoples alone nor the larger ones alone can impose a law on all the others.

For every other law, the alarm bell. Two thirds of a single delegation can suspend a law and send it to conciliation. Law adopted → Alarm: two thirds of one delegation → Suspended → Conciliation → If it fails: two thirds of the Kongres.
Registers estimated from the population of each people’s States (vote engine of the portal).

chapters.title: Direct democracy
text: The people have the last word. 150,000 citizens or twelve States can put any law passed by the Kongres to a referendum.
Citizens can change the Constitution. 300,000 signatures within eighteen months put a revision to the vote.
A double majority. A revision passes only with a majority of voters and a majority of the States: 27 of 52.
Four voting Sundays a year. The same day everywhere in the Confederation.

chapters.title: One language
text: One language, three standards. The južnoslovenski jezik is written in three regional standards, equal in dignity and in law. Zapadni (western): Skupščina narodov; Središñi (central): Narodni Sabor; Istočni (eastern): Sãbranie na narodite.
One alphabet of 32 letters. Ã for the Bulgarian schwa, Ě for the old jat’, Ñ and Ļ for the soft n and l, X for dž.
Latin and Cyrillic, letter for letter. Each letter has its Cyrillic twin: a text passes from one script to the other without loss.

chapters.title: Living together
text: A semester of high school in a State of another people.
Military or civilian service, with six months of training outside one’s own State.
One football team per people, and a single Konfederalna Liga.
A common history that hides no crime and blames no people.
No confederal holiday commemorates a battle.
Founded on the freely renewed will to live together.

chapters.title: The symbols
text: The civil flag. A red band at the hoist, then blue, white and blue: the flag of every citizen.
The state flag. A golden sun of 36 rays bearing the winged lion in red, and Balkan textile friezes: for the institutions, the armed forces and embassies.
The golden winged lion. Emblem of the Confederation: the wings of the Balkan eagle on the Bulgarian lion.
Naš dom: Our home.
